name: Chicago Athletic Association Hotel
positioning: Restored Venetian Gothic landmark on Michigan Avenue, directly across from Millennium Park, part of The Unbound Collection by Hyatt
best_for: Design and history lovers who want a restored landmark building
Travelers who want to stay across from Millennium Park and the Art Institute

facts.text: The hotel is on Michigan Avenue in downtown Chicago, directly across from Millennium Park and the Art Institute.
The hotel is part of The Unbound Collection by Hyatt.
Rooms and suites feature intricate wood details, leather accents and custom finishes.
Beds have brass-bed-inspired headboards and Faribault Woolen Mill blankets.
Signature boxing-style robes are a nod to the hotel's athletic club roots.
The Millennium King Suite has two bedrooms, each with a king bed, plus a separate sitting area and Millennium Park views.
Founders Room 330 has a free-standing wrought iron bathtub overlooking Millennium Park.
Guests can borrow the hotel's custom Heritage Bicycles in season.
The Game Room, the original billiards room, is a bar with games including billiards, shuffleboard, chess and checkers.
Event spaces include a ballroom with stained glass and a space in a vintage basketball court.
Front desk staff are trained in the architecture and art of the building.
Pets are welcome with no weight limits, up to two per room.

highlights.text: The Venetian Gothic exterior gives way to a 19th-century interior of carved stone fireplaces, terrazzo floors and leaded glass, all freshly restored.
The Founders Suite has two working fireplaces, views of Millennium Park just below and original woodworking throughout.
The hotel was recognized with One Key in the 2025 MICHELIN Guide.
A Topgolf Swing Suite on the ground floor offers an indoor golf and interactive gaming simulator.
Cindy's sits atop the 13th floor under a glass atrium, with views of Millennium Park and Lake Michigan and an all-season terrace.

considerations.text: Rooms vary widely in size, with the most spacious overlooking Millennium Park.
The building is popular and can feel busy, especially on weekends, though the lobby is quiet in the morning.
A daily destination fee, subject to change, is applied to each room.
